description: A vice president of operations must decide how to respond to concerns that a team lead's feedback style is damaging collaboration, while setting the structure of coaching, meetings, and a repair process.

shared_context.S1: Several colleagues have raised concerns that Priyanka's feedback in group settings is abrupt and that follow-through between teams has become strained.
shared_context.S2: The team's documented project deliverables are generally on schedule, and no formal performance process has been opened.
shared_context.S3: Elena has authority to choose the response and record the resulting expectations for Priyanka and the team.
shared_context.S4: As part of the scheduled case review, Elena hears directly from Priyanka, the affected colleagues, and HR before recording the decision; each participant places any relevant agreement, observation, or policy record into the case record before Elena closes the review.

PF1.text: Marcus and Priyanka agreed after a difficult review six weeks ago that Priyanka would give written feedback within 24 hours of contentious meetings; Marcus has kept the messages documenting that agreement, but Elena has not seen them.

PF2.text: Priyanka experiences medication side effects that make meetings before 10:30 a.m. substantially harder; she asked her immediate supervisor last month to move recurring team meetings to 10:30, but the request was never escalated to Elena.

PF3.text: Jonah personally observed three separate meetings in which Priyanka interrupted a colleague and dismissed a concern before discussion could continue; he recorded the dates in his private notes but did not attach them to the complaint.

PF4.text: Tessa confirmed this week that HR's conduct-response policy calls for a 45-day structured coaching plan with separate interviews when output is on schedule and the concern is interpersonal conduct; the policy summary has not yet been added to Elena's case file.

acceptance_conditions: The response must be a structured coaching plan rather than a formal performance-improvement process.
The coaching plan must last exactly 45 days.
Separate interviews must be completed before any joint repair discussion.
A facilitated repair conversation must be scheduled for the affected colleagues and Priyanka.
Recurring team meetings must start at exactly 10:30 a.m.
The existing written-feedback agreement must be made an explicit protocol.
The settlement must identify the observed conduct pattern as a reason for the repair process.

content_checks.C7: decisions['conduct_pattern_documented'] == True and 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF3' in revealed and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in credited_facts

decisive_facts.why: The documented prior agreement changes the response from general coaching advice to an explicit requirement for written feedback within 24 hours.
Priyanka's medication side effects change the recurring meeting start from an unspecified normal schedule to exactly 10:30 a.m.
The three dated observations change the concern from a general complaint to a documented conduct pattern requiring a facilitated repair conversation.
The confirmed HR policy changes the response to a structured coaching plan lasting exactly 45 days with separate interviews before repair.
